A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and their main text, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. Relocated material was matched across versions. Overflowing proof text in v2 was recoverable from the PDF.

before.justification: Section 8 and Figure 1 report original optimizer convergence experiments on f(x)=x^4 from three starting points.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix I adds a synthetic logistic-regression diagnostic and optimizer comparisons on a9a and mushrooms.

M1.justification: Algorithm 4 narrows the permitted AdGD parameter from gamma <= 1/sqrt(2) to gamma <= 1/2. Its update rule and the gamma=1/4 configuration underlying the refined analysis remain unchanged. The other algorithms, including the strongly convex adaptation, are retained.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained one-dimensional polynomial problem, v2 evaluates multidimensional logistic regression using constructed Gaussian-perturbed features and the real LIBSVM datasets a9a and mushrooms. This substantially broadens empirical coverage beyond the original synthetic objective.

E2.justification: The evaluated methods remain GD, (L0,L1)-GD, GD-PS, AdGD, (L0,L1)-STM, and (L0,L1)-STM-max. Figure 3 extends this same set to logistic regression. Newly discussed literature does not introduce additional empirical comparators.

E3.justification: The original polynomial protocol is unchanged. Added logistic experiments introduce starting-distance settings of 16 and 11000 for a9a and 5 and 28000 for mushrooms, retaining objective gap versus iteration. The synthetic diagnostic additionally measures Hessian norm against gradient norm.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds a targeted diagnostic of the relationship between Hessian and gradient norms in a constructed logistic problem. Figure 3 extends starting-distance sensitivity analysis to real datasets. The original polynomial sensitivity analysis remains unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added probability-bound derivation in Remark H.3 concerns theoretical convergence, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The three original Figure 1 panels are identical. New Figure 2 reports an approximately linear Hessian–gradient norm relationship in the constructed logistic example. Figure 3 adds convergence trajectories on two real datasets, favoring GD-PS and AdGD and showing no consistent advantage of the STM variants over GD. These are additional results under new conditions.

T1.justification: V1 Theorem 6.2 becomes v2 Theorem 6.1: the late-iteration AdGD bound changes from 4L0 exp(2L1D)D^2/N to 4L0D^2/(nu N), supported by a new large-step counting argument in Appendix G.2. Appendix D.1 adds a convergence-rate comparison derivation, and the clipping proof restores a missing exp(eta) factor. The new general-N condition contains a sign inconsistency with denominator positivity.

C1.justification: Section 1.3 substantially strengthens the AdGD contribution: an exponentially dependent complexity bound is replaced by one with leading term L0D^2/epsilon and polynomial transient dependence. The central claims concerning clipping, Polyak stepsizes, acceleration, and stochastic extensions otherwise remain.

C2.justification: V1 leaves removal of AdGD's exponential factor unresolved; v2 instead interprets the refined bound as evidence of adaptivity, while noting that D can exceed the initial distance. Appendix I adds applicability qualifications: logistic smoothness constants are difficult to determine, real datasets lack a clear linear Hessian–gradient relationship, and acceleration does not consistently help.

D1.justification: Appendix I specifies the new 50-dimensional feature construction, Gaussian perturbations, and labels with one negative example, and identifies LIBSVM as the real-data source. Existing polynomial settings are retained. Optimizer tuning and determination of the optimum for the new logistic experiments are not specified.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantial stochastic-optimization literature discussion and detailed comparisons with the proofs of Koloskova, Takezawa, and Chen. It acknowledges independent related results by Vankov et al. and expands attribution to Zhang et al. Additional variance-reduction and Polyak references appear, while Malitsky and Mishchenko (2023) is removed.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the document: numerical-experiment discussion moves to Appendix I, background discussion moves into an expanded Appendix A, and stochastic algorithms and strongly convex statements move to appendices. The main AdGD presentation is condensed and revised, with additional proof-comparison sections. These are structural changes beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: V2 adds a Hessian-versus-gradient scatterplot and a four-panel logistic-regression comparison. Figure 1 is retained with an expanded caption, while algorithm and theorem displays are redistributed between the main text and appendices. Some revised Appendix G definitions overflow the right page margin.

improvement.justification: The new counting argument and stronger late-iteration AdGD bound address the exponential-dependence limitation explicitly left unresolved in v1. Logistic-regression experiments broaden validation and reveal limits of acceleration, while expanded proof comparisons clarify novelty. These substantial gains outweigh the new general-N sign inconsistency, clipped proof definitions, and incomplete logistic-regression tuning details.
